sections.content:
Population change in Newcastle upon Tyne in 2032

The population in Newcastle upon Tyne is projected to increase from 306,402 people in 2022 to 334,700 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net international migration, which will increase the population by 50,302 people.

This is different to the majority of areas in England, where net internal migration is projected to be the biggest factor in population change.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Newcastle upon Tyne
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Newcastle upon Tyne, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 4,056, with 30,873 births and 26,817 deaths in Newcastle upon Tyne between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would increase the population in Newcastle upon Tyne by 1.3%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to reduce the population by 28,012, with 276,662 people moving to the area and 304,674 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Newcastle upon Tyne by 9.1%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to increase the population by 2,497, with 13,507 people moving to the area and 11,010 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Newcastle upon Tyne by 0.8%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 50,302, with 83,765 people moving to the area and 33,463 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Newcastle upon Tyne by 16.4%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Newcastle upon Tyne in 2032

The median age in Newcastle upon Tyne is projected to remain the same at 34 years between 2022 and 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 15% of the population in Newcastle upon Tyne are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 14% in 2022.

sections.title: The 50 to 59 age group are set to see the largest change in Newcastle upon Tyne between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Newcastle upon Tyne is projected to stay the same, at around 69%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 203 to 206 over the same time period.

This is below average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Newcastle upon Tyne?

In 2032, 19% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 21% in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Newcastle upon Tyne between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will stay around the same, at 5%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
